newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq urges Gulf states to back it against U.S.
newsitem.headline: Iraq urges Gulf states to back it against U.S.

text.p: Iraq on Friday asked member countries of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) to back it against "the evil forces" of the United States.

"There will be a GCC meeting on Saturday. And from here I urge the brethren in the Arab Gulf to take in their meeting a stand in support of Iraq against the evil and infidel forces of America," senior foreign ministry undersecretary Saad al-Faisel said in an interview carried by state-run television.

Pointing out that U.S. and allied warplanes had used Saudi and Kuwaiti bases in their patrols of the southern Iraq no-fly zone, he said he hoped Arab Gulf countries realised "the seriousness of this action which America undertakes from their territory".
The United States fired a total of 44 cruise missiles on Tuesday and Wednesday at air defence targets in southern Iraq to minimise Iraqi resistance to allied patrols over an expanded no-fly zone.
The U.S. attack came after Iraqi troops and armour intervened at the weekend in northern Iraq to help one Kurdish faction in its fight with another Kurdish group.
"What Iraq is being subjected to is a threat to Arab national security and in consequence it is a threat to Gulf security," Faisel said.
"When (the Gulf Arab states) take a positive decision (towards Iraq) they will be taking a stand in defence of themselves."
Baghdad has made repeated overtures particularly to Kuwait -- which it invaded in 1990 -- and Saudi Arabia since the 1991 Gulf War, but to no avail.
Faisel said it was time to forget the past and it would be "in nobody's interest to open past wounds".
He said he noted positive stands over the latest U.S. missile strikes against Iraq from the GCC member states United Arab Emirates (UAE), Qatar, Oman and Bahrain, apart from Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.
"I stress once again and ask (GCC countries) for a positive decision taking the nation's interest into consideration when meeting tomorrow," he said.
Saudi Arabia was the springboard for U.S.-led multinational forces in the Gulf War.
